hints.title: Identify Accepted Candidate Identifiers
hints.text: Determine candidate identifiers accepted under the priority hiring policy rather than aggregated row counts.

hints.title: Compute Running Sums by Experience
hints.text: Use a window cumulative sum over candidates partitioned by experience and ordered by salary ascending.

hints.title: Filter and Union Candidate IDs
hints.text: Select employee identifiers from seniors within seventy thousand and juniors within remaining leftover budget.

hints.title: Complete Query
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH RankedCandidates AS (
    SELECT
        employee_id,
        experience,
        salary,
        SUM(salary) OVER(PARTITION BY experience ORDER BY salary, employee_id) AS running_salary
    FROM Candidates
),
Seniors AS (
    SELECT employee_id, running_salary
    FROM RankedCandidates
    WHERE experience = 'Senior' AND running_salary <= 70000
),
Juniors AS (
    SELECT employee_id, running_salary
    FROM RankedCandidates
    WHERE experience = 'Junior'
      AND running_salary <= (70000 - COALESCE((SELECT MAX(running_salary) FROM Seniors), 0))
)
SELECT employee_id FROM Seniors
UNION ALL
SELECT employee_id FROM Juniors;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting candidates within each tier
complexity.space: O(N) for ranked candidate common table expressions
complexity.notes: Filters candidates by running salary thresholds and outputs individual ids.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recomputing sums without analytic functions triggers multiple table scans.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window functions offer single-pass cumulative budgeting.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should output exact employee identifiers in any order using UNION ALL.

import pandas as pd

def number_of_seniors_and_juniors_to_join_the_company_ii(candidates: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    seniors = candidates[candidates['experience'] == 'Senior'].sort_values(by=['salary', 'employee_id'])
    seniors['running'] = seniors['salary'].cumsum()
    accepted_seniors = seniors[seniors['running'] <= 70000]
    spent = accepted_seniors['running'].max() if not accepted_seniors.empty else 0
    
    juniors = candidates[candidates['experience'] == 'Junior'].sort_values(by=['salary', 'employee_id'])
    juniors['running'] = juniors['salary'].cumsum()
    accepted_juniors = juniors[juniors['running'] <= (70000 - spent)]
    
    return pd.concat([accepted_seniors[['employee_id']], accepted_juniors[['employee_id']]], ignore_index=True)
solutions.approach: Pandas candidate filtering by cumulative budget
